prompt: Where does a screen reader get what it says about a web page?
hint: It does not look at the screen.

choices.text: From the pixels on the screen, by text recognition
choices.why: Some tools can do that as a fallback; a screen reader reads the page's structure.

choices.text: From the accessibility tree the browser builds
choices.why: Right. Roles, names and states, through the system's accessibility interface.

choices.text: From the HTML source, downloaded again
choices.why: It never sees the source; it sees what the browser made of it.

choices.text: From the CSS, which says how each element looks
choices.why: Style is not in the tree, which is why the red border said nothing.

prompt: Match each screen reader to where it runs.
hint: Two are built into a phone or a Mac.
right_distractors: a browser extension that reads only Chrome

prompt: Testing with NVDA, you press H in a text field and an h is typed instead of jumping to a heading. Why?

choices.text: The page has disabled NVDA's shortcuts
choices.why: A page cannot switch NVDA's commands off; this is NVDA's own behaviour.

choices.text: NVDA is in focus mode, where letter keys type
choices.why: Right. It enters focus mode on its own in a text field; in browse mode H means next heading.

choices.text: H is a VoiceOver command and NVDA does not have it
choices.why: H is NVDA's next-heading key, in browse mode.

choices.text: The page has no headings for H to jump to
choices.why: It has one, and that would produce a message, not a typed letter.

prompt: Why does this course capture no screen reader speech?
hint: Where does a screen reader run?

choices.text: Screen readers forbid recording in their licences
choices.why: Not the reason; NVDA is open source.

choices.text: Speech is the same in every reader, so one capture would add nothing
choices.why: It differs by reader, version, settings and browser.

choices.text: The lab has no desktop for one to run on
choices.why: Right. The tree is captured instead, and inventing speech would be a false capture.

choices.text: Playwright blocks screen readers from attaching to Chromium
choices.why: Playwright has nothing to do with it.

prompt: In book.html's tree the name field appears as textbox with no name. Why, when "Your name" is printed next to it?
hint: Next to it on screen is not tied to it.

choices.text: The text is too far from the field for the browser to see
choices.why: Distance does not matter; only a relationship in the markup does.

choices.text: Nothing in the markup relates the text to the field
choices.why: Right. A <label for> is the relationship, and 1.3.1 asks for it.

choices.text: Text fields never have names in the tree
choices.why: book3.html's has one: textbox "Your name".

choices.text: The tabindex hides the field's name
choices.why: tabindex changes the order, not the name.

prompt: Order the sources of an accessible name from the one checked first to the one checked last.
items: a <label>, an alt, or the element's content

prompt: A button shows the word Book and carries aria-label="Submit". What is its accessible name, and who is hurt?

choices.text: Book; aria-label is ignored when there is visible text
choices.why: It is not ignored; it wins over the content.

choices.text: Book Submit, joined; nobody is hurt
choices.why: The first source wins; they are not joined.

choices.text: Submit; somebody using voice control who says Book
choices.why: Right. The visible label is not in the name, which fails 2.5.3 Label in Name.

choices.text: Submit; sighted mouse users, who see a different word
choices.why: They see Book and click it; the name does not reach them.

prompt: A team adds role="button" to book.html's div, and nothing else. What changes for a keyboard-only user who can see?
hint: ARIA changes what the tree says.

choices.text: Nothing: the div still cannot take the focus or answer a key
choices.why: Right. A role is a promise in the tree; tabindex and key handlers are what keep it.

choices.text: The div joins the tab order, because buttons are focusable
choices.why: Native buttons are; a role does not make a div focusable.

choices.text: It answers Enter but still not Space
choices.why: It answers neither: no handler was written.

choices.text: It becomes fully a button, since the role tells the browser to add the behaviour
choices.why: The browser adds no behaviour for a role.

prompt: The first rule of ARIA: if a ___ HTML element already does what you need, use it instead of adding ARIA to another element.
hint: <button> rather than a div with role="button".

prompt: Why is the empty <span role="alert"> already in book4.html when the page loads?
hint: What does a screen reader watch?

choices.text: An empty alert is read out on load, to warn the user in advance
choices.why: Nothing is announced while it is empty.

choices.text: A region that exists first gets its changes announced
choices.why: Right. One inserted together with its text is often not announced at all.

choices.text: axe requires every form to have an alert, or it fails
choices.why: No rule requires one; book3.html passed without.

choices.text: The CSS needs it to draw the red border
choices.why: The border hangs off aria-invalid on the field.

prompt: Match each part of book4.html's fix to what it does.

pairs.right: makes the message the field's description
marks the field's state as invalid

right_distractors: adds the field to the tab order

prompt: Which criterion does the word "Error:" at the start of the message help book4.html meet?
hint: The border was only a colour.

choices.text: 2.4.7 Focus Visible
choices.why: That is about the focus indicator.

choices.text: 1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum)
choices.why: The colour's contrast was never the problem.

choices.text: 1.4.1 Use of Color
choices.why: Right. The error is carried by words as well as by colour.

choices.text: 2.1.1 Keyboard
choices.why: Book was already operable in book3.html.

prompt: What does charter.js take from the page to write its checklist?

choices.text: A recording of NVDA reading the page
choices.why: No screen reader runs in the VM.

choices.text: axe's list of violations
choices.why: It does not run axe.

choices.text: The roles and names in the accessibility tree
choices.why: Right. What the browser will hand the reader, to be checked against what is heard.

choices.text: The visible text of every paragraph
choices.why: Paragraphs and plain text are filtered out.

prompt: How many things to listen for did charter.js list for book4.html?
hint: It printed the count before the file.

prompt:
A search page shows "12 results" in a

after each search, without moving the focus. In the tree after a search, the line reads paragraph: 12 results. What is missing?

choices.text: Nothing: the text is in the tree, so a reader announces it
choices.why: In the tree is not announced; the user would have to go and find it.

choices.text: An alert, since every message must interrupt the user
choices.why: A count is not urgent; alert is for errors to deal with now.

choices.text: A polite live region, such as role="status", present from load
choices.why: Right. 4.1.3 Status Messages, announced without moving the focus.

choices.text: Moving the focus to the paragraph so it gets read
choices.why: That works and drags the user away from the search box.

prompt: axe passes, tab.js shows a sensible order, and tree.js shows every name. What can only the screen reader session still find?
hint: Present and right are different things.

choices.text: A missing alt attribute on an image
choices.why: axe and the tree both report that.

choices.text: A positive tabindex
choices.why: The tab walk shows that.

choices.text: Whether the names and the speech make sense to a listener
choices.why: Right. A name can be present and wrong, and only a person judges that.

choices.text: Whether the text contrast is above 4.5:1
choices.why: Contrast is axe's strongest check, and a reader cannot see colour.

prompt: A release note reads "Booking page: WCAG 2.2 AA, axe clean". Which version of the claim matches what lessons 12 to 15 did?
hint: Name the tools, the layers and the readers.

choices.text: Accessible: Lighthouse 90 and no axe violations
choices.why: That is the first layer alone, and a score.

choices.text: axe clean, tab order and tree checked by script, a manual session with a named reader
choices.why: Right. Three layers, each named, which is what the requirement asked for.

choices.text: WCAG 2.2 AAA, since every A and AA criterion passed
choices.why: AA does not imply AAA.

choices.text: Conforms to eMAG, which replaces WCAG in Brazil
choices.why: eMAG binds government sites and is built on WCAG; it replaces nothing.
